title: Query features in 0.0.48
body:
Query features in 0.0.48
Maintainer handoff for the two `GraphObjectManager` query features added in 0.0.48:
1. **Quantified predicates** (`any{}` / `none{}`) over a to-many `@GraphRelationship` in `where{}`.
2. **Filtered vector search** — caller `where{}` predicates AND-ed into `loadNearest`.

Both are verified end-to-end against Neo4j, FalkorDB, and Memgraph.

---

title: Feature 1 — `any{}` / `none{}` over a to-many relationship
body:
Feature 1 — `any{}` / `none{}` over a to-many relationship
```kotlin
loadAll<PropositionView> { where { mentions.any { resolvedId eq entityId } } }
loadAll<PropositionView> { where { mentions.any { resolvedId inList entityIds } } }
loadAll<PropositionView> { where { mentions.none { resolvedId eq entityId } } }
loadAll<PropositionView> { where { mentions.any { role eq "SUBJECT"; resolvedId eq entityId } } } // correlated
```

### Design decisions (and what diverged from the original spec)

- **No codegen change.** The spec assumed the KSP codegen would need to emit a quantifier accessor
  for `List<>` relationships. It doesn't: codegen already emits a to-many relationship as the target
  `Properties` object (e.g. `MentionProperties("mentions")`, alias = the relationship field name),
  identical to a to-one. So `any`/`none` are **pure runtime context-extensions on `NodeReference`**
  (`GraphQueryDsl.kt`) — the receiver is the target `Properties`, so the target's fields are in scope
  inside the block. Lower-risk, and works for any generated or hand-written DSL.
- **`any{}` is the explicit form of the existing flat shorthand.** `mentions.resolvedId eq id`
  already worked: `CypherGenerator.groupConditionsByAlias` converts a property condition whose alias
  is a relationship name into a `RelationshipCondition`, rendered via `grammar.filteredExistenceCheck`.
  `any{}` builds the same condition; the block just makes per-element correlation explicit and gives
  a home to `none{}`.
- **`none{}` = `negate` flag + portable `NOT (...)`.** Added `negate: Boolean` to
  `WhereCondition.RelationshipCondition`; `CypherGenerator.buildRelationshipCondition` wraps the
  positive inline condition in `NOT (...)` at every return site. This is portable across engines —
  no new per-grammar method — because the positive form is already engine-correct.
- **Reuses the existing per-grammar existence rendering** (`filteredExistenceCheck`), which already
  varies by engine and is battle-tested by the relationship-filter DSL.

### Generated Cypher (per engine), `mentions.any { resolvedId eq $id }`

| Engine   | Rendering |
|----------|-----------|
| Neo4j 5  | `EXISTS { (proposition)-[:HAS_MENTION]->(mentions) WHERE mentions.resolvedId = $id }` |
| Memgraph | `size([(proposition)-[:HAS_MENTION]->(mentions) WHERE mentions.resolvedId = $id | 1]) > 0` |
| FalkorDB | `CALL { WITH proposition OPTIONAL MATCH (proposition)-[:HAS_MENTION]->(mentions) WHERE … RETURN count(mentions) AS _ec0 }` → `_ec0 > 0` |
| Neptune  | inherits openCypher (CALL-subquery form); engines without subquery support throw per the grammar default |

`none{}` wraps the above in `NOT (...)`.

### Code

- `query/dsl/GraphQueryDsl.kt` — `RelationshipCondition.negate`; `any`/`none` context-extensions.
- `query/dsl/PropertyReference.kt` — `inList` infix (readable alias for the backtick `` `in` ``).
- `query/dsl/CypherGenerator.kt` — `finalize()` NOT-wrapping at the relationship-condition returns.

---

title: Feature 2 — filtered vector search: `loadNearest(..) { where { } }`
body:
Feature 2 — filtered vector search: `loadNearest(..) { where { } }`
```kotlin
loadNearest(PropositionView::class.java, queryObject, queryVector, topK = 20) {
    where { query.proposition.contextId eq ctx; query.proposition.status eq "active" }
}
```

### Design decisions

- **Property predicates only, on the projected root — by construction.** The vector path filters
  *after* projection, where the root has been rebound to a map (`proposition {…} AS proposition`).
  Property predicates render as `proposition.contextId = $p` (map-key access) and AND straight into
  the existing post-projection `WHERE` — **byte-identical to the load path's predicate rendering**,
  reusing `CypherGenerator.buildWhereClause`. This is also why the documented FalkorDB
  vecf32-Pointer quirk isn't re-triggered: the filter is a scalar on a map, not a pattern on the node.
- **Relationship-quantifier predicates are rejected here (for now).** They render as
  `EXISTS { (proposition)-[…] }`, which can't traverse a map. The manager detects any
  relationship predicate (`hasRelationshipPredicate`) and throws `UnsupportedOperationException`
  with a clear message rather than emitting broken Cypher. See follow-ups.
- **`topK` semantics unchanged** — it's the index's `k`; post-filtering may yield fewer rows.
- Shared execution: both `loadNearest` paths funnel through `executeVectorSearch(...)`
  (rows → `Scored<T>` + snapshot).

### Generated Cypher (Neo4j) — vector + property predicate

```cypher
CALL db.index.vector.queryNodes('Proposition_embedding_vector', $_vectorTopK, $_vectorQuery)
YIELD node, score
WITH node AS proposition, score AS _score
WITH proposition { … } AS proposition, [(proposition)-[:HAS_MENTION]->(mentions) | …] AS mentions, _score
WHERE proposition.contextId = $param_proposition_contextId_0
  AND proposition.status = $param_proposition_status_1
RETURN { value: { proposition: proposition, mentions: mentions }, score: _score } AS row
ORDER BY _score DESC
```

(FalkorDB/Memgraph differ only in the vector head; the property `WHERE` is identical.)

### Code

- `query/GraphViewVectorSearchBuilder.kt` — `build(..., callerWhere)`: ANDs the caller clause into
  the post-projection filter.
- `query/GraphViewQueryBuilder.kt` — `buildVectorQuery(.., callerWhere)`.
- `manager/GraphObjectManager.kt` — `loadNearest(graphClass, queryObject, vector, topK, threshold, spec)`
  overload; renders caller conditions, guards relationship predicates, merges bindings;
  `executeVectorSearch(...)` helper; `hasRelationshipPredicate(...)`.

title: `@PropertyBag` — 0.0.50
body:
`@PropertyBag` — 0.0.50
Maintainer handoff for `@PropertyBag`: persist an open `Map<String, *>` field on a `@NodeFragment`
as **flat, prefixed node properties**, round-tripped on save and load. Verified end-to-end on Neo4j,
FalkorDB, and Memgraph.

```kotlin
@NodeFragment(labels = ["Proposition"])
data class PropositionNode(
    @NodeId val id: String,
    val text: String,
    @PropertyBag val metadata: Map<String, Any?> = emptyMap(),   // -> metadata.<key> properties
)
```

`metadata = {"source": "wiki", "score": 3}` persists as `metadata.source = "wiki"`,
`metadata.score = 3` alongside `id`/`text`. Mirrors Spring Data Neo4j's `@CompositeProperty` (kept as
the alias `@CompositeProperty`). Unlike `@JsonPacked`, entries are real properties — filterable and
indexable.

title: Semantics
body:
Semantics
- **Stored key:** `"${prefix.ifEmpty{fieldName}}${delimiter}${key}"`. `prefix` decouples the graph
  namespace from the field name; `delimiter` defaults to `.`.
- **Value types:** each value must be a storable Neo4j primitive or **homogeneous array** (String,
  Number, Boolean, temporal, or arrays/lists thereof). A non-storable value (nested map, object,
  heterogeneous list) throws `IllegalArgumentException` at save **naming the key** — never emits
  Cypher the driver will reject.
- **Multiple bags per fragment** are supported (each with its own prefix). Overlapping prefixes —
  one a delimiter-prefix of another (`a.` vs `a.b.`) — are rejected at model build, since a stored
  key would otherwise be claimed by two bags on load.
- **Read type asymmetry (documented quirk):** a `Map<String, Any?>` reads back driver-mapped types,
  so an `Int` written returns as `Long`. A typed bag / value converter is a follow-up.
- **Empty / null:** an empty bag writes nothing (and clears stale keys); reads back `emptyMap()`.

title: Clear-stale-then-set — and the one limitation
body:
Clear-stale-then-set — and the one limitation
On update, keys removed from the map must disappear from the node. drivine diffs the **session
snapshot**: `removedKeys = oldBag.keys − newBag.keys`, emitted as static
`REMOVE n.`metadata.<key>``. The save statement is a single `MERGE … SET … REMOVE …`.

**Limitation (by design):** stale removal needs the prior state, which only exists for
session-tracked objects (the normal `load → mutate → save` flow). A **detached save** — `new`-ing an
object and saving it without ever loading it — upserts the current keys but cannot know which old
keys to remove (there is no portable "remove all keys under this prefix" in Cypher without dynamic
key removal / APOC). This matches how dirty tracking already treats detached objects. Load before
mutating if you need stale keys cleared.

title: Load — `.*` projection + client-side reconstruction
body:
Load — `.*` projection + client-side reconstruction
A bag's keys are open, so the declared-field projection can't name them. Bag-bearing fragments are
projected with `.*` (the same portable path polymorphic fragments already use), surfacing every node
property. `TransformPostProcessor.reconstructPropertyBags` then walks the result — root fragment and
each relationship target, recursively through nested views — collecting prefix-matched keys into the
bag's map field before Jackson deserialization, and dropping the flat keys.

*Cost note:* `.*` ships **all** properties back, including any embedding vector on the node. For
vector-heavy fragments loaded in bulk this is overhead; filtering to just the prefixed keys in Cypher
isn't portable (needs dynamic key access / APOC). Acceptable for v1; an opt-in narrow projection is a
possible follow-up.

title: Filtering — the `key()` accessor
body:
Filtering — the `key()` accessor
The generated query DSL emits a `PropertyBagReference` (not a scalar) for a bag field, so individual
keys are filterable:

```kotlin
loadAll<PropositionView> { where { proposition.metadata.key("source") eq "wiki" } }
```
→ `WHERE proposition.`metadata.source` = $p`

`CypherGenerator` backtick-quotes a property segment containing a dot (the stored bag key); plain
fields and relationship aliases are untouched, and the parameter name still derives from the raw
path. Composes on the load path **and** inside `loadNearest { where { } }` (the 0.0.49 filtered
vector path) for free.

title: Generated Cypher (per engine — identical; only declared-field handling differs)
body:
Generated Cypher (per engine — identical; only declared-field handling differs)
```cypher
-- save (update dropping "score")
MERGE (n:Proposition {id: $id})
SET n.text = $text, n.`metadata.source` = $_bag0
REMOVE n.`metadata.score`

-- load (projection)
MATCH (n:Proposition)
RETURN { .*, labels: labels(n) } AS result   -- .* surfaces metadata.* for reconstruction
```

(FalkorDB / Memgraph backtick the same way; `.*` map projection is portable on all three.)

title: Code
body:
Code
- `annotation/PropertyBag.kt` — `@PropertyBag` + `@CompositeProperty` alias.
- `model/FragmentField.kt`, `model/PropertyBagModel.kt`, `model/FragmentModel.kt` — detect bags,
  partition them out of `fields` into `propertyBags` (with resolved `storedPrefix`), overlap guard.
- `query/FragmentMergeBuilder.kt` — bag expansion (backtick-quoted SET), clear-stale REMOVE, value
  validation; `previousObject` threaded from the snapshot via `GraphObjectMergeBuilder` /
  `GraphViewMergeBuilder`.
- `query/GraphViewProjectionAssembler.kt`, `query/FragmentQueryBuilder.kt` — bag fragments use `.*`.
- `mapper/TransformPostProcessor.kt` — `reconstructPropertyBags`.
- `query/dsl/PropertyReference.kt` — `PropertyBagReference.key(name)`.
- `query/dsl/CypherGenerator.kt` — `renderPropertyPath` backtick-quoting.
- `drivine4j-codegen/.../QueryDslGenerator.kt` — emits `PropertyBagReference` for bag fields.

| Capability | Neo4j | FalkorDB | Memgraph |
|---|---|---|---|
| save → load round-trip (multi-entry, list values) | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| update clears stale key | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| bags through `@GraphView` (root + relationship target) | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| `where { metadata.key(k) eq v }` filter | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |

body:
Tests

- `manager/PropertyBagCrossEngineTest` (Neo4j / FalkorDB / Memgraph) — round-trip, stale removal,

title: Language support
body:
Language support
Works fully from **Kotlin and Java**.

- **Persistence (save / load / clear-stale / validation):** language-agnostic (Jackson + reflection).
  `@PropertyBag` on a private-field Java fragment is recognized and round-trips — covered by
  `JavaPropertyBagTest` and a Java save→load on Neo4j.
- **Typed `key()` DSL accessor:** the Kotlin (KSP) generator emitted it in 0.0.50; the **Java (APT)
  generator emits it as of 0.0.51** (`drivine4j-codegen-java`), so the generated Java DSL exposes
  `node.metadata().key("source")`. Covered by a compile-testing test
  (`PropertyBagCodegenTest`) asserting the generated `…Properties` source. Before 0.0.51, Java
  consumers filtered via the string WHERE form (`"n.`metadata.source` = 'wiki'"`), which still works.

title: Follow-ups
body:
Follow-ups
1. **Typed bags / value converters** (`Map<String, String>`, custom converters) — v1 is
   `Map<String, Any?>` with driver-mapped reads (the Int→Long asymmetry).
2. **Narrow load projection** — avoid shipping the whole property set (incl. vectors) for bag
   fragments; needs portable filtered-key access.
3. **Detached-save stale clearing** — currently requires session tracking (see limitation above).
4. **Catch-all / overflow mode** (`prefix=""` meaning "every undeclared property → bag") — deferred;
   riskier (must not swallow reserved/internal props).
5. **Annotation-driven index over a bag key** — a user can still
   `RangeIndexSpec("Proposition", "metadata.source")` via `SchemaCatalog` manually.
6. **Refactor** `QueryDslGenerator.generateFragmentPropertiesClass` (now hefty) into focused
   emitters — quality-only, post-landing.

title: Limit & skip — DB-side pagination with GraphView root cardinality — 0.0.52
body:
Limit & skip — DB-side pagination with GraphView root cardinality — 0.0.52
Backfilled. The file existed but was empty; this reconstructs the handoff from `15fde11` and the
behaviour the cross-engine tests pin. Superseded for large or changing result sets by keyset
pagination — see [0.0.75-index-aware-keyset-pagination.md](0.0.75-index-aware-keyset-pagination.md).

title: The contract
The key design decision: LIMIT bounds roots, not rows
body:
The key design decision: LIMIT bounds roots, not rows
For a `@GraphView`, `limit(n)` bounds **root entities**, and each returned view keeps its
relationships fully populated.

This is only true because of how views are projected: relationships are pattern comprehensions inside
the projection, so one root is exactly one row. A join-shaped query would have made `LIMIT 1` on a
root with two children return a half-populated object — the classic ORM pagination bug. Here the
cardinality question never arises, and the cross-engine test pins it: limiting to a single root that
has two mentions still returns both mentions.

Anyone changing the projection strategy away from pattern comprehensions has to revisit this
guarantee, which is the main reason this note exists.

title: Semantics worth knowing
body:
Semantics worth knowing
- Without `orderBy`, the subset is an arbitrary `<= n` — standard Cypher, not a Drivine choice. Pair
  `limit` with `orderBy` for a deterministic top-N.
- `count(…)` ignores `limit`/`skip` in the same spec: it answers "how many match", not "how many
  would this page return".
- `loadNearest` takes no limit — `topK` is already its bound.
- `limit(0)` returns empty; `skip` past the end returns empty. Both are asserted rather than assumed.
- `limit` and `skip` require `n >= 0`.

title: Why offset pagination is not the end of the story
body:
Why offset pagination is not the end of the story
`skip(n)` makes the engine walk and discard `n` rows, so cost grows with page depth, and any
concurrent insert shifts every subsequent page — a row can be seen twice or skipped entirely. That is
acceptable for shallow, static result sets and poor for deep or live ones, which is what `seek`
(0.0.74) exists to solve. `seek` and `skip` are mutually exclusive by construction.

title: Code map
body:
Code map
- `manager/GraphObjectManager.kt` — `applyPagination`, appending SKIP/LIMIT and merging the bindings.
- `query/dsl/GraphQueryDsl.kt` — `limit` / `skip` on `GraphQuerySpec`.
- `query/dsl/JavaQueryBuilder.kt` — the Java fluent equivalents.

title: Tests
body:
Tests
- `LimitSkipDslTest` — spec-level behaviour without a database.
- `LimitSkipCrossEngineTest` — Neo4j, FalkorDB and Memgraph: top-N, disjoint pages, the root
  cardinality guarantee (a limited root keeps its full collection), the edge cases, and that `count`
  ignores `limit`. Later extended with the keyset cases from 0.0.74/0.0.75.

title: Generated `loadNearest { where { } }` view extension — 0.0.54
body:
Generated `loadNearest { where { } }` view extension — 0.0.54
Closes follow-up #3 from `docs/query-features-0.0.48.md`. The codegen now emits a per-`@GraphView`
reified `loadNearest` extension that injects the view's `…QueryDsl.INSTANCE`, matching the ergonomics
of the generated `loadAll { }`.

> **Also in this build:** an audit found `count` was the one remaining DSL method still requiring
> `…QueryDsl.INSTANCE` (it had a hand-written reified `count<T, Q>(queryObject, spec)` but no generated
> wrapper). The codegen now emits `count(spec)` per view too — **ungated** (count applies to any view),
> so `count<RaisedAndAssignedIssue> { where { } }` works without `INSTANCE`. With this, every
> DSL-spec method — `loadAll`, `deleteAll`, `count`, `loadNearest` — has a generated INSTANCE-injecting
> form.

```kotlin
// before — had to pass both type args + INSTANCE
graphObjectManager.loadNearest<PropositionView, PropositionViewQueryDsl>(
    PropositionViewQueryDsl.INSTANCE, vector, topK = 20, threshold = 0.7
) { where { proposition.contextId eq ctx; mentions.any { resolvedId eq id } } }

// now
graphObjectManager.loadNearest<PropositionView>(vector, topK = 20, threshold = 0.7) {
    where { proposition.contextId eq ctx; mentions.any { resolvedId eq id } }
}
```

> **Signature extended in 0.0.79.** The generated wrapper now also takes `searchK` (the HNSW beam
> width, for over-fetching) and `partitionLabel` (targeting a per-partition index), both defaulting to
> null. The shape below is otherwise unchanged, and the additions are source-compatible. See
> [0.0.79-vector-search-k.md](0.0.79-vector-search-k.md) and
> [0.0.79-vector-partitioning.md](0.0.79-vector-partitioning.md).
>
> ```kotlin
> public inline fun <reified T : PropositionView> GraphObjectManager.loadNearest(
>     vector: List<Float>,
>     topK: Int,
>     threshold: Double? = null,
>     searchK: Int? = null,
>     partitionLabel: String? = null,
>     noinline spec: GraphQuerySpec<PropositionViewQueryDsl>.() -> Unit,
> ): List<Scored<T>>
> ```

title: What's generated
body:
What's generated
For each `@GraphView` whose **root fragment has a `@VectorIndex`**, alongside the existing
`loadAll`/`deleteAll` extensions (same generated file):

```kotlin
public inline fun <reified T : PropositionView> GraphObjectManager.loadNearest(
    vector: List<Float>,
    topK: Int,
    threshold: Double? = null,
    noinline spec: GraphQuerySpec<PropositionViewQueryDsl>.() -> Unit,
): List<Scored<T>> = loadNearest(T::class.java, PropositionViewQueryDsl.INSTANCE, vector, topK, threshold, spec)
```

Exactly the wrapper pattern the generated `loadAll(spec)` already uses, delegating to the existing
`loadNearest(graphClass, queryObject, vector, topK, threshold, spec)` manager method.

title: Decisions
body:
Decisions
- **Only the filtered (spec) form.** The non-filtered `loadNearest<T>(vector, topK, threshold)` is a
  hand-written reified extension (`GraphObjectManagerExtensions`) needing no query object — not
  regenerated.
- **Gated on `@VectorIndex` on the root fragment** (the chosen option). A view with no embedding
  can't be searched (the runtime `VectorIndexResolver` would throw), so no `loadNearest` is emitted
  for it — verified: `SampleVectorView` gets one, `RaisedAndAssignedIssue` does not.
- **No overload clash.** The generated `loadNearest(vector, topK, threshold, spec)` (no queryObject,
  has a spec lambda) is distinct from the hand-written `loadNearest<T>(vector, topK, threshold)` (no
  spec) and the manager `loadNearest<T, Q>(queryObject, …, spec)` (queryObject first). Confirmed:
  `loadNearest<SampleVectorView>(vec, topK) { … }` binds to the generated one, and the sample module
  compiles it.
- **Kotlin codegen only.** The Java APT path uses the fluent `JavaQueryBuilder`, not generated
  extension functions; a Java `loadNearest` builder method is a possible follow-up.
- **Property-disambiguation variant out of scope** — multi-embedding views use the explicit method
  (the manual filtered form has no property variant either). Follow-up.

title: Code
body:
Code
- `drivine4j-codegen/.../QueryDslGenerator.kt` — `generateLoadNearestExtensionFunction` (mirrors
  `generateLoadAllExtensionFunction`), added to the view's file when `rootFragmentHasVectorIndex(...)`
  is true. KotlinPoet auto-imports `Scored`, `GraphQuerySpec`, `List<Float>`, etc.

title: Tests
body:
Tests
- `drivine4j-sample/.../GeneratedLoadNearestTest` — asserts the **real KSP-generated** source:
  `SampleVectorViewQueryDsl` contains the `loadNearest` extension with the right `…INSTANCE`
  delegation; `RaisedAndAssignedIssueQueryDsl` (non-vector) contains none. The sample module also
  compiles the generated code (proving imports + no ambiguity).
- `manager/FilteredVectorSearchNeo4jTest` — a Neo4j round-trip calling the generated-shape wrapper
  (`loadNearest<PropositionView>(QUERY, topK) { where { property + any{} } }`) and asserting identical
  `Scored<T>` results to the explicit `loadNearest(graphClass, INSTANCE, …)` call. (The underlying
  filtered `loadNearest` is already cross-engine tested; this proves the wrapper delegates.)

body:
Follow-ups
1. Property-disambiguation generated variant (multi-embedding views).
2. Java `loadNearest` builder method for parity with the Kotlin generated extension.

title: `FULLTEXT_INDEX` schema item kind — 0.0.60
What it does
body:
What it does
Adds `FullTextIndexSpec(label, properties, name?, analyzer?)` — an `IndexSpec`, so it flows through
`SchemaCatalog.items` (`indexes + constraints`), `IndexManager.ensure/find/recreate/drop`, and
`SchemaManager` exactly like the range and vector kinds. Multi-property like `RangeIndexSpec` (unlike
single-property `VectorIndexSpec`). `defaultName()` → `"${label}_${properties.joinToString("_")}_fulltext"`.

title: Design decisions (and why)
body:
Design decisions (and why)
- **Multi-property, one spec.** A fulltext index over `[title, body]` is one searchable analyzed
  field, so it is modelled as a single spec with a property list — matching how Neo4j and Memgraph
  natively express it. FalkorDB, which has no multi-property fulltext primitive, decomposes it (below).

- **`analyzer` is drift *only where the engine reports it back*.** `matchesShape` now follows one
  uniform rule for every shape attribute: **null on the introspected side means "unobservable", not
  "mismatch".** A `FullTextIndexSpec.analyzer` is treated as drift only when the spec sets one *and*
  introspection surfaces one to compare against. Neo4j is the only engine that both accepts an
  analyzer and reports it (`fulltext.analyzer` in the index `options.indexConfig`); FalkorDB and
  Memgraph report null, so a spec's analyzer is silently unverified there rather than drifting
  forever. This is the "never report drift we can't observe" principle the vector `similarity`
  attribute already used — generalized in the `matchesShape` KDoc.

- **Empty `indexConfig` when no analyzer.** On Neo4j, a spec with no analyzer emits
  `OPTIONS {indexConfig: {}}` and lets the engine apply its own default (`standard-no-stop-words`),
  rather than hard-coding a default that could drift across Neo4j versions.

- **Explicit names honoured where supported; the consumer binds them as parameters.** Neo4j and
  Memgraph fulltext indexes are named, and `effectiveName` / an explicit `name` is respected — this
  matters for the RAG consumer, which binds the index name as a query parameter (`$fulltextIndex`)
  and needs the created name to be predictable. FalkorDB fulltext indexes are unnamed
  (`supportsNamedItems = false`), so `name` is ignored there and `SchemaItemInfo.name` is null.

title: The FalkorDB per-property reassembly (the fiddly part)
body:
The FalkorDB per-property reassembly (the fiddly part)
FalkorDB has no named, multi-property fulltext primitive. It exposes:

```cypher
CALL db.idx.fulltext.createNodeIndex('<Label>', '<prop>')   -- one property per call
```

and rejects re-indexing an already-fulltext property (`Attribute 'x' is already indexed`) — exactly
like its range path. So `createIndex`:

- Emits **one procedure call per property** *missing* from the label's existing fulltext coverage
  (using the `existing: SchemaItemInfo?` the manager already passes, identical to the range/vector
  logic). Extending `[name]` to `[name, description]` emits only the `description` call.
- On **introspection**, `parseIndexRows` fans a single `db.indexes()` row (one row per label, whose
  `types` map marks each property's index types) back into **one** `FULLTEXT_INDEX` item covering
  *all* `FULLTEXT`-typed properties of the label. Without this reassembly, a `[title, body]` spec —
  created as two calls — would never match one introspected item and would report drift on every
  `ensure`. `matchesIdentity` uses coverage (`containsAll`), not set-equality, for the same reason
  range does.
- **Drop** is per-property: `DROP FULLTEXT INDEX FOR (n:<Label>) ON (n.<prop>)`, so dropping a
  fulltext index never disturbs a range index (or another property's fulltext) on the same label.

A property can legitimately carry both `[RANGE, FULLTEXT]`; the range and fulltext fan-outs read the
same row independently and produce two distinct items, one per kind.

title: Backend support
body:
Backend support
| Engine   | Create DDL | Named | Multi-prop | Analyzer | Status |
|----------|-----------|-------|------------|----------|--------|
| Neo4j 5  | `CREATE FULLTEXT INDEX \`<name>\` IF NOT EXISTS FOR (n:<Label>) ON EACH [n.<p1>, n.<p2>] OPTIONS {indexConfig: {\`fulltext.analyzer\`: '<a>'}}` | ✅ | ✅ native | ✅ emitted + drift-checked | ✅ verified |
| Memgraph | `CREATE TEXT INDEX <name> ON :<Label>(<p1>, <p2>)` (note: `TEXT`, not `FULLTEXT`; no `IF NOT EXISTS`) | ✅ | ✅ native | ⚠️ ignored (not reported back) | ✅ verified |
| FalkorDB | `CALL db.idx.fulltext.createNodeIndex('<Label>', '<prop>')` — one call per missing property | ✗ unnamed | ⚠️ decomposed to per-property calls, reassembled on read | ⚠️ ignored | ✅ verified |
| Neptune / openCypher | `UnsupportedSchemaGrammar` throws, as for every other kind | — | — | — | ✅ throws |

### Introspection shapes (verified against live containers)

- **Neo4j** `SHOW INDEXES` → `type = "FULLTEXT"`, analyzer at `options.indexConfig["fulltext.analyzer"]`.
- **Memgraph** `SHOW INDEX INFO` → positional row `["label_text (name: <name>)", "<Label>", ["<p1>","<p2>"], <count>]`.
  The index name is parsed out of the type string; the label may arrive colon-prefixed on 3.11+ and
  is normalized like the other Memgraph kinds.
- **FalkorDB** `CALL db.indexes()` → one row per label, `types` map e.g. `{title: [FULLTEXT], age: [RANGE, FULLTEXT]}`.

title: Writing `@VectorIndex` properties as the engine's native vector type on save — 0.0.61
body:
Writing `@VectorIndex` properties as the engine's native vector type on save — 0.0.61
Maintainer handoff for the write-side vector fix: embeddings saved through `GraphObjectManager`
(`save` / `saveAll`) are now stored as the engine's native vector type, so FalkorDB's vector index
actually picks them up.

title: The bug
body:
The bug
Drivine wrapped the query vector in `vecf32(...)` on the **read** side for FalkorDB
(`FalkorDbCypherGrammar.vectorSearchHead`) but did nothing on the **write** side —
`FragmentMergeBuilder` rendered every property uniformly as `SET n.$field = $field`. On FalkorDB a
vector index only indexes a property stored as the native `Vectorf32` type; a plain array assigned to
that property is **silently accepted and silently left out of the index** (see the upstream report,
[FalkorDB#2233](https://github.com/FalkorDB/FalkorDB/issues/2233)). So saving an embedding through
`GraphObjectManager.save()` wrote a plain array, the index stayed empty, and `loadNearest` returned
nothing.

The asymmetry was masked because the existing cross-engine tests hand-wrote the literal in raw Cypher
(`VectorSearchCrossEngineTest`, `seed(pm) { "vecf32($it)" }`) rather than saving through the manager —
so `save()` → `loadNearest` on FalkorDB had no coverage at all.

Neo4j and Memgraph index a stored array directly and are unaffected; their write path stays
byte-identical.

title: The fix — three seams, mirroring the read side
body:
The fix — three seams, mirroring the read side
1. **Model awareness.** `FragmentField.vectorIndexed` marks a `@VectorIndex` field; `FragmentModel`
   populates it during field extraction (Kotlin + Java reflection, alongside how it already detects
   `@PropertyBag`) and exposes `FragmentModel.vectorFieldNames`.

2. **Write-side grammar hook.** `CypherGrammar.vectorPropertyLiteral(param): String` — default
   `"$param"` (plain bind), overridden to `"vecf32($param)"` in `FalkorDbCypherGrammar`. A derived
   `CypherGrammar.wrapsVectorLiteral` (true only when the literal wraps) gates the batch fallback with
   a single source of truth.

3. **Apply in the merge builder.** `FragmentMergeBuilder` branches the `SET` clause: a vector field
   with a non-null value is written as `n.$field = ${grammar.vectorPropertyLiteral(field)}`. **The
   binding is unchanged** — only the RHS differs. The grammar is threaded from `GraphObjectManager`
   (`persistenceManager.grammar`) through `GraphObjectMergeBuilder.forClass` → the fragment/view merge
   builders; it is nullable and defaults to plain output, so unit tests that construct the builder
   directly stay byte-identical.

### Null embeddings

`vecf32(null)` is invalid on FalkorDB, so a null vector value is **never wrapped** — it falls through
to a plain `SET n.$field = $field`, which clears the property, exactly matching normal null semantics.

### Batch path (`saveAll`)

The UNWIND batch upsert (`SET n += row.props`) cannot wrap one property in `vecf32(...)`. So a root
fragment carrying a `@VectorIndex` field **falls back to the per-item save path on engines that wrap**
(`grammar.wrapsVectorLiteral`, i.e. FalkorDB) — mirroring how a `@PropertyBag` root already falls
back. On Neo4j / Memgraph the UNWIND path is retained (a plain array indexes fine there), so batch
throughput is unchanged for them.

title: Backend support
body:
Backend support
| Engine | Write form | Batch (`saveAll`) | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| FalkorDB | `SET n.embedding = vecf32($embedding)` | per-item fallback (UNWIND can't wrap) | ✅ verified: save → indexed → `loadNearest` finds it |
| Neo4j | `SET n.embedding = $embedding` (unchanged) | UNWIND (unchanged) | ✅ verified, byte-identical write |
| Memgraph | `SET n.embedding = $embedding` (unchanged) | UNWIND (unchanged) | ✅ verified, byte-identical write |

title: Read-back
body:
Read-back
A `vecf32`-stored property loads back through `FalkorDbResultMapper` as a plain `List` of numbers, so
`gom.load(...)` reconstructs the `List<Float>?` embedding field normally — covered by an explicit
round-trip assertion.

body:

- `FragmentField.vectorIndexed`, `FragmentModel.vectorFieldNames` (+ Kotlin/Java detection).
- `FragmentMergeBuilder` — the `SET`-clause branch + null guard; nullable `grammar` param.
- `GraphObjectMergeBuilder.forClass`, `FragmentMergeBuilderAdapter`, `GraphViewMergeBuilder`
  (root + relationship-target fragment builders) — grammar threaded through.
- `BatchSaveOperations` — vector-bearing-root fallback gated on `wrapsVectorLiteral`; grammar threaded
  into the per-item merge builder.
- `GraphObjectManager` — passes `grammar` at the `save` and `saveAll` (`BatchSaveOperations`) sites.

title: Tests
body:
Tests
- `query/grammar/VectorSearchGrammarTest` — `vectorPropertyLiteral` / `wrapsVectorLiteral` per engine.
- `query/VectorMergeBuilderTest` — model recognizes the vector field; FalkorDB wraps (binding
  unchanged); Neo4j plain; null never wrapped; no-grammar plain.
- `manager/SaveThenVectorSearchCrossEngineTest` — **the actual gap**: saves through the manager
  (single `save`, view-root `save`, and batch `saveAll`) with no raw `vecf32` in the fixture, then
  `loadNearest` ranks/prunes and the embedding round-trips. Runs on FalkorDB (fails before the fix,
  passes after), plus Neo4j and Memgraph as regression guards.

### Test-hygiene notes (worth knowing)

Two non-obvious things surfaced writing the cross-engine test; neither is a product bug:

- **Session dirty-tracking vs. out-of-band delete.** A reused `GraphObjectManager` snapshots saved
  objects; if the graph is cleared with `DETACH DELETE` behind the session's back, the next `save` of
  the same object sees no dirty fields and skips the embedding write — leaving the index empty. The
  test builds a fresh manager per scenario (models a fresh process).
- **Memgraph vector index + delete.** Memgraph does not purge a `DETACH DELETE`d node from its HNSW
  vector index; a later search trips over it ("Trying to get labels from a deleted node") even after
  the index is recreated. The test avoids inter-scenario deletes, MERGE-ing stable ids instead. (A
  candidate upstream report if it recurs for the consumer.)

title: `@GraphProperty` — map a fragment field to a differently-named node property — 0.0.62
Why
body:
Why
A consumer promoting structural keys out of an open metadata map into typed fields has those
properties on-disk in **snake_case** (`container_section_id`, `sequence_number`, `root_document_id`, …)
and hand-written traversal Cypher that reads them by those exact names. Idiomatic Kotlin fields are
camelCase. Without a name override the only options were a full data migration or not promoting the
fields — this removes the dilemma.

title: The core split: field name is identity, property name is on-disk
body:
The core split: field name is identity, property name is on-disk
`FragmentField` gains `propertyName` (defaults to `name`). The rule threaded through every seam:

- **Identity** (`FragmentField.name`) — bind-parameter names, result-map keys, DSL accessor names,
  session/dirty tracking. Unchanged by an override.
- **On-disk** (`FragmentField.propertyName`) — the written `SET` target, the read projection *source*,
  the id `MERGE`/`WHERE` key, the DSL WHERE left-hand side, and the schema index property.

`FragmentModel.from` reads `@GraphProperty` via both Kotlin reflection (constructor-property
annotations) and Java-field reflection, so Java fragments work too. It exposes
`FragmentModel.nodeIdProperty` (the id field's on-disk name).

title: Seams (code map)
body:
Seams (code map)
| # | Seam | File | What it does |
|---|------|------|--------------|
| 1 | **Write** | `FragmentMergeBuilder` | `SET n.<propertyName> = $<name>` — property decoupled from bind-param. `@VectorIndex` wraps the **param** (`vecf32($name)`) while assigning `<propertyName>`. `@NodeId` MERGE key uses `nodeIdProperty`. |
| 1b | **Batch write** | `BatchSaveOperations` | The UNWIND `SET n += row.props` remaps `row.props` keys to on-disk names and MERGEs on `nodeIdProperty` (no-op remap without overrides). |
| 2 | **Read, concrete** | `FragmentQueryBuilder` | Projection aliases `<name>: n.<propertyName>`; id `WHERE` uses `nodeIdProperty`. |
| 3 | **Read, polymorphic `.*`** | `TransformPostProcessor.reconstructFragmentData` | After concrete-type resolution, renames each override key (`container_section_id` → `containerSectionId`) before `convertValue`. Recurses views. No-op on the concrete path (already field-keyed). |
| 4 | **DSL where** | `PropertyReference` + codegen (`drivine4j-codegen` KSP, `drivine4j-codegen-java` APT) | The generated accessor keeps the field name; its `PropertyReference` carries the **on-disk** name, so `where { chunk.containerSectionId eq x }` renders `chunk.container_section_id = $param`. |
| 5 | **Schema specs** | `FragmentSchemaScanner` | `@VectorIndex` / `@RangeIndex` / `@FullTextIndex` / `@Unique` (property- **and** class-level) build specs on the on-disk name; error messages still name the Kotlin field. |
| 6 | **GraphViews** | `GraphViewProjectionAssembler`, `NestedViewProjector` | Embedded root/relationship-target fragment projections alias `<name>: src.<propertyName>`; the polymorphic `.*` rename (seam 3) already recurses views. |
| 7 | **Vector search read** | `FragmentVectorSearchBuilder`, `VectorIndexResolver` | The `loadNearest` fragment projection aliases field ← property; the resolver searches (and derives the index name from) the **on-disk** embedding name. |

Seam 7's `FragmentVectorSearchBuilder` projection was the one non-obvious miss — vector search has
its own RETURN map, separate from `FragmentQueryBuilder`, and without the alias an overridden
embedding loaded back null (ranking still worked, so it failed quietly). Called out here because it's
the trap the next similar feature will re-encounter.

title: The `@VectorIndex` + `@GraphProperty` + `vecf32` interaction (flagged)
body:
The `@VectorIndex` + `@GraphProperty` + `vecf32` interaction (flagged)
All three now key on the on-disk name consistently, so the loop closes:

- schema creates the index on `<propertyName>` (`FragmentSchemaScanner`);
- `save()` writes `SET n.<propertyName> = vecf32($<name>)` on FalkorDB (`FragmentMergeBuilder`);
- `loadNearest` searches `<propertyName>` and derives the index name from it (`VectorIndexResolver`),
  and the projection reads it back into the field (`FragmentVectorSearchBuilder`).

Verified on FalkorDB and Neo4j (`GraphPropertyVectorTest`): index on `embedding_vec`, `vecf32` write
to `embedding_vec`, `loadNearest` ranks and round-trips. **No consumer action needed** — an overridden
embedding "just works", and the Neo4j/Memgraph derived index name shifts to `<label>_<onDiskName>_vector`
(matches on both create and search sides).

title: Interactions / edge cases
body:
Interactions / edge cases
- **`@GraphProperty` + `@PropertyBag`** on one field → rejected at `FragmentModel.from` (a bag manages
  its own prefixed names).
- **Collision** — two fields resolving to the same on-disk name (via overrides, or an override
  colliding with another field's default) → rejected at `FragmentModel.from`, naming both fields.
- **`@NodeId` override** — flows into the MERGE key, the load `WHERE`, and the batch UNWIND MERGE key.
- **Dirty tracking / session snapshot** — keyed on the Jackson field-name tree, so unaffected; the
  polymorphic `.*` rename (seam 3) restores field names before any snapshot comparison, so no path
  sees on-disk keys.

title: One documented deviation (DSL bind-param name)
body:
One documented deviation (DSL bind-param name)
The DSL bind-param derives from the property path in `CypherGenerator.generateParamName`. With the
on-disk name now in the `PropertyReference`, the internal param becomes `param_chunk_container_section_id_0`
rather than `…_containerSectionId_0`. This is entirely internal — the bindings-map key and the `$ref`
change together and stay aligned, so filtering is correct. Keeping it field-derived would mean
threading a separate param-basis through every `WhereCondition`, which isn't worth it.

| `@NodeId` override (save + `load(id)`) | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| Polymorphic `.*` subtype override | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |

title: Standalone query DSL for bare `@NodeFragment` — 0.0.67
Using it — exact syntax and the trip-ups (read this first)
What it generates
body:
What it generates
Per `@NodeFragment`, a `<Fragment>QueryDsl` — a [`NodeReference`] at the fragment root alias `"n"`
(matching `FragmentQueryBuilder.nodeAlias`), exposing the node's property references (honoring
`@GraphProperty` on-disk names and `@PropertyBag`), an `INSTANCE`, and `instanceOf()` support for
sealed/abstract fragments. `where { query.<prop> … }` renders `n.<prop> …`; `instanceOf<Sub>()` renders
`n:<labels>`. Parameterized bindings (`$param_*`) — the same path the view DSL uses; no string splice.

**The runtime already supported this** — `loadAll(class, Q, spec)` / `count` / `deleteAll` route through
`GraphObjectQueryBuilder.forClass` → `FragmentQueryBuilder` (with `viewModel == null`), and the Java
`query(F).filterWith(FQueryDsl).…` fluent builder delegates to the same. This change is **codegen-only**:
the KSP and APT processors previously only visited `@GraphView`.

`loadNearest` for a `@VectorIndex` fragment needs no new codegen — the hand-written non-filtered reified
`loadNearest<T>(vector, topK, threshold)` already works for any `T`, fragments included.

title: The sealed-hierarchy overload subtlety (Kotlin)
body:
The sealed-hierarchy overload subtlety (Kotlin)
A reified `inline fun <reified T : Fragment> loadAll(spec)` is ambiguous for `loadAll<Sub>` when the
base also has one (a subtype satisfies `T : Base`, and neither candidate is more specific). So the
Kotlin generator emits the `loadAll`/`count`/`deleteAll` **extensions only for "root" fragments** — those
with no generated `@NodeFragment` supertype (sealed/abstract bases and standalone fragments). Every
fragment (including subtypes) still gets its **`QueryDsl` class**. Consequences:

- `loadAll<Base> { where { query.baseProp; query.instanceOf<Sub>() } }` — works (base extension).
- `loadAll<StandaloneFragment> { where { query.prop } }` — works.
- `loadAll<Sub> { }` — resolves to the base extension, typed `List<Sub>`, filterable on **base**
  properties.
- Filtering a subtype by its **own** property uses the explicit 3-arg form:
  `loadAll(Sub::class.java, SubQueryDsl.INSTANCE) { where { query.subProp eq … } }` — unambiguous, and
  the `SubQueryDsl` exists for exactly this.

Java has no extension functions, so **no ambiguity** — a `<F>QueryDsl` is generated for every fragment
and used explicitly via `query(F.class).filterWith(FQueryDsl.class)`.

title: Backend support
body:
Backend support
The generated DSL is engine-agnostic (it feeds the same runtime); verified cross-engine
(Neo4j / FalkorDB / Memgraph) for `loadAll` / `count` / `deleteAll`, `where` (incl. a `@GraphProperty`
on-disk name), `instanceOf()` on a sealed base, and per-node polymorphic dispatch.

  - `QueryDslGenerator` — `fragmentClasses`; `generateFragmentDsl`; the property-getter loop extracted

body:

body:
Consumer impact
`embabel-agent-rag-graph` can query its promoted node types directly — e.g. all chunks in a section by
a `@GraphProperty` field, or a sealed `ContentElementNode` narrowed with `instanceOf()` — instead of a

title: Follow-ups
body:
Follow-ups
1. **Filtered fragment `loadNearest`** — `loadNearest(F, FQueryDsl.INSTANCE, vector, topK) { where { } }`
   (vector search + a caller predicate on a bare fragment). The runtime `loadNearest(class, Q, spec)`
   currently requires a `@GraphView`; non-filtered fragment vector search already works.
2. **`loadAll<Sub>` ergonomics** — the subtype-explicit-form workaround is documented; a nicer typed
